root_idea.summary: A cessation-oriented root: ceasing or desisting, with a related causative sense of making something cease.
root_idea.development: The supplied evidence distinguishes the Form I negative construction meaning “not cease,” hence continued action, from positive uses of abstaining and of stilling or extinguishing. No Maqāyīs or Mufradāt development discussion was supplied.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form فَتِئَ rather than the Quranic imperfect surface form تَفْتَؤُا۟.

senses.definition: To cease or leave off doing something.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the verb appears after an oath in a construction understood as negative, meaning “you will not cease remembering Joseph.” Form I in this sense is characteristically used in negative phrases.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To forget an affair; to abstain or desist from it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded with عَنْهُ in the construction فَتِئَ عَنْهُ. This use is reported as generally occurring in negative phrases.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To still, quiet, abate, or allay something; to make someone cease from an affair; to extinguish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A complete, active verb distinct from the negative Form I construction; the evidence illustrates its use both for making a person cease from an affair and for extinguishing a fire.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form I cessation use and its Quranic negative construction are represented.
The use for forgetting and abstaining or desisting is represented.
The positive use for stilling, abating, making cease, and extinguishing is represented.

cautions: The Quranic form is an imperfect active Form I occurrence whose negative interpretation is carried by the oath construction rather than by an overt لا immediately before the verb.
